review_candidates.title: Program Director
review_candidates.description: Head and Neck Cancer Alliance — Program Director Job Description Reports To: Executive Director FLSA Status: Exempt, Full-Time Location: Remote (U.S.-based; East coast hours); occasional travel required for conferences, partner meetings, and the annual Survivorship Symposium Direct Reports: No direct reports currently; may include program coordinators, interns, and/or contract staff, as assigned, in the future About the Alliance The Head and Neck Cancer Alliance ("the Alliance") is a national nonprofit organization that provides hope and support to individuals affected by head and neck cancer; raises awareness about prevention and early detection; and advocates for improved patient outcomes. Core programs include Oral, Head and Neck Cancer Awareness Program, the annual Survivorship Symposium conference, the Ambassador Program, educational webinars, and patient and caregiver support services (including the financial assistance program, peer-to-peer mentoring, and online support communities). Position Summary The Program Director is a key member of the Alliance's leadership team, responsible for the strategic development, implementation, and evaluation of the Alliance's programs. Reporting to the Executive Director, the Program Director ensures that the Alliance's programs advance the organization's mission, meet stated goals and outcomes, and reflect current best practices in patient support, awareness, survivorship care, and education. This role also serves as a visible external representative of the Alliance to partners, funders, healthcare professionals, and the broader head and neck cancer community. Key Responsibilities Program Management & Strategy Develop, implement, and evaluate the Alliance's core programs to ensure they advance the organization's mission and meet defined objectives and outcomes. Partner with a board liaison from the medical community to remain informed about head and neck cancer and emerging research and trends. Direct the annual Survivorship Symposium (patient conference) in partnership with clinical and academic collaborators, overseeing content development, speaker recruitment, logistics (in-person and virtual formats), site selection, and post-event evaluation. Oversee scope of work, hiring, and supervision of external event planner. Lead the Alliance's educational programming, including leading the Program Committee and scheduling regular meetings, identifying expert speakers and survivors, scheduling and planning webinars with assistance of external AV consultant, collaborating with marketing manager to drive outreach and registration. Manage the Ambassador Program, a group of 80+ survivor and caregiver volunteers, including recruitment, training, and connection to opportunities to represent the Alliance at speaking engagements, events, in the media, and in research initiatives. Maintain up-to-date training materials, monitor WhatsApp chat group, and respond to requests for Ambassador involvement by matching Ambassadors with activities. Lead planning and execution of Oral, Head and Neck Cancer Awareness Program, a screening and education initiative; includes new site assistance, coordination of the materials/resources to sites, and development of screening kit resources. Oversee patient-facing support services, including the Peer-to-Peer mentor and the external partner (Imerman Angels) relationship, financial assistance program, and the Online Support Community, including training for community moderators. Establish and monitor program budgets, timelines, and performance metrics; report regularly on progress and outcomes to the Executive Director and Board of Directors. Partnership & Funder Engagement Serve as a liaison to the Alliance's partner organizations, such as Imerman Angels, Inspire Online Support Community, American Cancer Society’s HPV Roundtable, dental organizations, and other allied patient advocacy organizations that interact with the Alliance’s programs. Serve on advisory boards and committees as needed. Represent the Alliance at conferences, advocacy meetings, and community events at the local and national level. Organizational Leadership Serve as an active member of the Alliance's leadership team, contributing to strategic planning, annual goal-setting, and organization-wide decision-making. Uphold the key internal values of the Alliance team, including collaboration with trust, commitment to growth, work/life balance, and open communication. Supervise and support program staff, interns, and contractors as assigned. Perform other duties as assigned in support of the Alliance's mission. Qualifications Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in public health, nonprofit management, healthcare administration, or a related field preferred. Minimum of 5-7 years of progressive experience in nonprofit program management, healthcare, or patient advocacy, including experience managing multiple concurrent programs. Demonstrated experience planning and executing conferences, symposia, or large-scale events, ideally in a healthcare or survivorship context. Experience working with volunteers, survivors, and/or patient populations with sensitivity, discretion, and compassion. Strong track record of building and managing partnerships with industry supporters, donors, healthcare institutions, clinicians, and nonprofit stakeholders. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to represent the organization professionally to diverse audiences. Strong project management skills, including budget oversight and outcome tracking. Proficiency with standard office, database, and virtual meeting technology; experience with CRM or donor/program databases a plus. Ability to travel periodically for conferences, partner meetings, and the Survivorship Symposium. Passion for the Alliance's mission and a commitment to serving the head and neck cancer community with empathy and integrity. Work Environment & Physical Requirements This is a remote position requiring reliable home-office infrastructure, a dedicated working space, and the ability to work independently while collaborating with a distributed team. The role requires occasional travel, including multi-day trips for the Survivorship Symposium and other events, some of which may require standing, walking, and assisting with event setup. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. East coast office hours preferred. Compensation & Benefits Salary is commensurate with experience and will be shared with qualified candidates during the interview process. In lieu of health care and other benefits, the Alliance offers a competitive leave package and salary. Specific terms will be outlined in an offer of employment. Equal Opportunity Employer The Head and Neck Cancer Alliance is an equal opportunity employer. The Alliance does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other status protected by applicable law. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds, including survivors and caregivers, to apply. To Apply Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter describing their interest in and qualifications for this role to info@headandneck.org. We appreciate your interest and regret that we are unable to reply to every applicant; if your qualifications are a strong match, we will follow up to schedule an interview.

review_candidates.title: Head of Engineering, POS Application Platform
review_candidates.description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why Kenya Powering that scale takes engineering talent well beyond our home markets - which is where Kenya comes in. Kenya is where our next chapter begins. Following our acquisition of Sumac Microfinance Bank, we're preparing to go live - which means the people we hire here help build a business from its first day, not inherit one. How we execute in Kenya will shape how we approach every market we enter after it, making this one of the most consequential engineering mandates in the business right now. This is the natural extension of our mission: to drive financial inclusion, and help millions of business owners and individuals across the African continent achieve financial happiness and success. We already have a small number of team members in engineering based out of Kenya, who have become central to how we build and run our platform globally. So, now we are now looking for our Head of Engineering, POS Apps to join us in India. About The Role More than 6 million businesses run their financial lives through Moniepoint - and the primary way they interact with us every single day is through a POS device. For most of our merchants, that device is their business. It is how they accept payments, how they access credit, and how they track their finances. Everything those devices are capable of, in terms of speed, reliability, and developer quality, flows from the engineering platform this role leads. We are building a dedicated POS Application Platform function: the foundational Kotlin-based engineering layer that sits beneath every POS product at Moniepoint. Think of it as the operating system for our POS engineering organisation - the standards, frameworks, tooling, and architectural backbone that every POS engineer across the business builds on top of. This is not a feature team. It is a platform team in the truest sense, and the Head of Engineering for POS Application Platform is the technical owner of that layer. We currently operate across five POS device types from multiple OEM manufacturers, all running on Android. The engineering challenges here span device governance, developer experience, platform reliability, foundational frameworks, and adoption across a distributed set of POS engineers working in separate product squads. And the scope is growing. We have a UK entity live, a cross-border payments product in market, and a microfinance bank acquisition which just finalized in Kenya. The platform you build will become the foundation for tens of millions of businesses across multiple markets to accept payments, access financial services, and grow. If you have spent your career going deep on POS systems and you want to build the platform that underpins one of Africa's most consequential fintech businesses during its expansion, this is the role. Collaborate with OEM partners and the POS hardware team when new device types are introduced, ensuring the application layer is ready to support them from day one. Build and scale the POS platform team, including hiring, mentoring, and structuring for growth as the platform expands internationally. Translate platform decisions into business impact, working closely with Product, Payments, and Business leadership across markets. Establish and continuously improve engineering processes, tooling standards, CI/CD pipelines, and developer productivity metrics across the POS engineering community. Direct, hands-on experience building software that runs on Point-of-Sale terminal devices. This means engineering on the device itself — the application layer — not server-side integrations with POS systems. This is a non-negotiable requirement and candidates without it will not be considered. Strong working knowledge of EMV standards (Europay, Mastercard, Visa) and experience navigating payment certification processes such as PCI DSS and P2PE. Candidates without this will not be considered. Deep Android engineering expertise in Kotlin and Java. The POS application layer at Moniepoint is Android-based and there are no exceptions to this requirement. Proven experience building internal engineering platforms, shared libraries, developer tooling, or foundational frameworks used by other engineering teams — not just consumer-facing feature products. Experience governing or architecting across multiple POS device types from different hardware manufacturers, with an understanding of how OEM integrations and device management work at scale. Experience building or maturing platform engineering functions, including establishing engineering processes, tooling strategies, and cross-squad governance structures. Demonstrated ability to scale engineering teams and build the organisational layer beneath you — leaders who can grow into and around the role you are hiring into. Experience at a company processing high volumes of financial transactions in a regulated environment. Fintech background is strongly preferred. Familiarity with terminal management systems and device observability tooling is a strong advantage. Backend engineering experience in Java or Spring Boot is a strong plus given the breadth of the platform and the integration surface it sits on. Experience working directly with OEM vendors on hardware specification and integration is a bonus. Exposure to C or C++ is a plus — one of our device variants uses C. Experience at Series A or B stage startups alone is unlikely to reflect the scale and complexity required for this role. Cultural Alignment We assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation. Customer Obsession: Deep empathy for the people depending on the platform — whether that is a merchant in Lagos trying to accept a payment, or a POS engineer blocked by missing tooling. You make trade-offs explicit, reason from first principles, and consistently produce solutions that are better than typical. Systemisation: You convert recurring decisions into repeatable mechanisms. You reduce cognitive load for others. You strengthen institutional memory and improve engineering quality at scale. Urgency: You move with disciplined speed. You act without waiting for permission when you are within scope. You escalate early when risk exceeds your authority. You remove friction and close loops. Performance without integrity is unacceptable. Stage 2: Technical Round focused on core technical strengths and depth in Android/Kotlin Stage 3: System Design - You will be asked to solve complex system design problems to assess your technical and architectural skills, with a particular focus on POS and mobile platform architecture and payment systems. Stage 4: Technical and Architectural Leadership - An interview with one Head of Engineering focused on leadership skills and attributes. Stage 5: CTO Interview - A conversation with our CTO assessing first-principles thinking, problem-solving under ambiguity, clarity of thought, and cultural alignment. All of it is aimed at one thing. When a founder or an investor asks ChatGPT, Perplexity or Google how raising capital works and who to raise with, we want Pairs quoted back, and we want what gets quoted to be good. VC Content Interns you brief, edit and grow into full-time hires. Content structured so AI answer engines and journalists quote us, with share of voice tracked and SEO fundamentals underneath. You are a fit if you Have built and run a brand end to end that we can open: a named brand where you set the voice, made the content, ran the channels, and know the before and after numbers from memory.
